title: SSO deployment playbook + min-privilege model review - Aurora Biotech
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Aurora Biotech team through an SSO/SAML + SCIM deployment playbook and mapped an RBAC least-privilege model to SCIM groups. Discussed certificate rotation, SCIM rate limits, break-glass, audit log exports, KMS/BYOK options, and data residency implications for a Private deployment. Agreed next steps: share SAML metadata, provide SOC2 pack, run SCIM sync POC, and draft role-to-group mapping doc.
topics: SCIM provisioning cadence and rate limits
RBAC role taxonomy and group mappings
Audit logs retention/export and SIEM integration
KMS / BYOK options and encryption at rest
Data residency and Private deployment considerations
next_steps: Redwood to send SAML metadata + ACS/EntityID endpoints (Maya)
Aurora to share IdP test tenant + contact for SCIM connector (Lina)
Redwood to circulate SOC 2 + ISO docs and SOC-2 summary (Jordan)
Schedule 2-hour SCIM sync POC with dev account (tentative week of 11/10)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-29 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Aurora Head of IT), Priya Kumar (Aurora SecOps), Ethan Ross (Aurora Platform)

---
Summary (auto): go-through of SSO + SCIM implementation playbook and mapping RBAC roles to SCIM groups; log forwarding and KMS questions surfaced.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hi everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:04] Lina Gomez: yeah loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:06] Maya Chen: cool, i'll kick us off with quick agenda — go over SSO/SAML metadata exchange, scim provisioning flow, role mapping for least-privilege, then multi tenancy / data residency notes and finally operational items like cert rotation, logs and k-m-s. Jordan will jump in on the technical bits.
[00:23] Jordan Patel: hey all, quick note i'm gonna share a small diagram in chat that shows SP v IdP initiated flows — it'll help as we talk about assertions and group claims.
[00:31] Priya Kumar: perfect, we use Okta as our IdP in prod and we'll likely test on a dev Okta tenant.
[00:36] Maya Chen: great — for the playbook we typically recommend: 1) exchange metadata and test SAML login, 2) enable SCIM in a test tenant and verify provisioning of a handful of users and groups, 3) map SCIM groups to Redwood roles, 4) enforce MFA upstream and disable password fallback after cutover.
[00:52] Ethan Ross: quick Q — can you support both SP and IdP initiated? our SSO patterns vary across teams.
[00:57] Jordan Patel: yes both — Redwood supports SP and IdP initiated. note though if you rely on IDP-initiated deep links sometimes attributes may vary; we recommend including groups in the SAML assertion to avoid a second round-trip.
[01:12] Lina Gomez: groups in the assertion — we've had trouble with group size in the past though, like huge group dumps. is there a recommended pattern?
[01:18] Jordan Patel: totally. two patterns: 1) include a scoped set of groups in the assertion for authn/authorization (e.g., role groups only), or 2) use SCIM to provision groups and then map by group id on the Redwood side. SCIM is more scalable for orgs with large group graphs.
[01:34] Priya Kumar: ok, we want least-privilege. how granular are Redwood roles? we don't want a million tiny roles.
[01:40] Maya Chen: here's our common taxonomy: Org Admin (full), Project Admin (deploy/config), Developer (invoke, read/write), Read-only / Auditor, Billing. That's a starting point — you can have custom roles too but we usually map to groups.
[01:53] Ethan Ross: so we'd map AD groups to those role buckets via SCIM?
[01:57] Jordan Patel: yes — typical mapping: AD group 'rbac-admins' -> Org Admin, 'rbac-devs' -> Developer, 'rbac-audit' -> Read-only. We can also consume a custom attribute on the user for environment scoping if needed.
[02:12] Lina Gomez: how does deprovisioning work? we need immediate account disable when someone is offboarded.
[02:17] Jordan Patel: SCIM supports deprovision (active false) and we recommend webhooks for near-real-time updates, but if you need immediate lockout we support account disable on receipt of a SCIM user replace with active=false. typical latency is sub 60s, subject to provisioning jitter.
[02:33] Priya Kumar: that should be fine, will want to test it. also curious about rate limits and bulk ops — we have orgs with thousands of users.
[02:40] Jordan Patel: our SCIM endpoint supports bulk paging and we document rate limits per customer. for large initial syncs we recommend using our one-time bulk import flow or staggered batched provisioning. i'll include the limit table in the playbook.
[02:53] Maya Chen: moving on to cert rotation — okta and other IdPs force periodic rotation, how do we handle that on Redwood?
[02:59] Jordan Patel: we accept new certs via metadata exchange; there is a rotation window where both certs are active. recommend keeping both old and new metadata available at the IdP to avoid outages. we'll also support JWK endpoints for dynamic rotation if your IdP exposes it.
[03:17] Ethan Ross: what about break-glass accounts — a service account for emergency?
[03:21] Maya Chen: good call, we recommend a named break-glass account with a long, audited password stored in your vault and rotated monthly — also reduce its scope and require privileged approval to use. we can also whitelist it behind IP allowlist if you're using Private deployment.
[03:35] Priya Kumar: logs — we need audit logs shipped to our SIEM and a retention of 12 months for compliance.
[03:41] Jordan Patel: Redwood exports audit logs via S3 export or syslog/HTTPS push to your SIEM. retention in hosted product is configurable up to x years depending on plan; for Private deployments you control retention locally. we'll share exact schemas — note the audit trail includes token-level actions, who invoked model endpoints and configuration changes.
[04:00] Lina Gomez: is there PII in logs? we have to be careful.
[04:03] Jordan Patel: we try not to log full user-provided prompt payloads by default in audit logs; sensitive fields can be redacted. We'll work with you on policy — for PII we recommend token redaction and ensure logs go to your secure bucket.
[04:17] Maya Chen: KMS and BYOK — what's your preference?
[04:20] Priya Kumar: we prefer BYOK for keys at rest if possible.
[04:23] Jordan Patel: we support BYOK in private deployments and VPC setups via AWS KMS and customer-managed key rotation policies. For hosted customers we offer a customer-managed KMS integration option (bring-your-own-key) with limited HSM-backed flows. We'll attach the integration guide.
[04:38] Ethan Ross: does BYOK affect performance?
[04:40] Jordan Patel: negligible at request level — encryption/decryption happens at storage layer; per-request crypto isn't in the hot path. there is some overhead for key retrieval in rare paths.
[04:51] Lina Gomez: data residency — we need data to stay in eu-west-1 for certain workloads. can Redwood pin inference and logs to region?
[04:58] Maya Chen: yes — Private deployments or Dedicated capacity in a specific region can keep data in-region. Hosted API can be region pinned by account if we have the capacity in that region; for strict regulatory needs we recommend Private.
[05:11] Priya Kumar: SOC2 and ISO — we'd like to review artifacts and controls mapping for our audit.
[05:16] Jordan Patel: we'll share SOC2 type II report redacted and an ISO summary; for deep dives we can do an on-site or virtual security questionnaire. I'll attach the control matrix.
[05:28] Ethan Ross: are there specific logs for admin actions vs API invocations? we need both.
[05:32] Jordan Patel: yes admin events and API-level events are separate streams — admin events include configuration/role changes, API events include model invocation metadata. both are timestamped and include user identity.
[05:44] Lina Gomez: minor nit — does Redwood support SAML NameID format email and subject confirmation? our policies require email nameid.
[05:50] Jordan Patel: yes we support email NameID and persistent/unspecified formats; we can validate on the test tenant.
[05:57] Maya Chen: let's run through a quick Role Mapping checklist — Ethan, can you confirm your AD groups naming scheme?
[06:02] Ethan Ross: we have 'aurora-rw', 'aurora-admins', 'aurora-audit' and env-specific suffixes like '-stg' and '-prod'.
[06:09] Jordan Patel: suggestion: map prod groups only to prod roles and use SCIM group attribute or prefix to disambiguate. we'll put examples in the mapping doc.
[06:21] Priya Kumar: what about service accounts that need API keys instead of SSO?
[06:25] Jordan Patel: we support long-lived service tokens for programmatic access, but they should be tied to a least-privilege role and rotated. For extra safety, we recommend short-lived tokens minted via an OAuth flow that requires an IdP assertion.
[06:39] Maya Chen: can you do conditional access? like block certain geos or require MFA for high-priv roles?
[06:44] Jordan Patel: conditional is enforced at the IdP layer mostly (Okta/OneLogin). Redwood can enforce policies like IP allowlist for Private deployments and we can require session timeout shorter for admin-level roles. We'll document the interplay.
[06:59] Lina Gomez: we've had issues where SCIM group names change and mappings break — is there a more stable key to map on?
[07:05] Jordan Patel: map on group id if possible — scim group id is stable. If your IdP supports an immutable external id attribute, use that as canonical.
[07:17] Ethan Ross: any gotchas with multi-tenant workspaces? our R&D orgs are separate business units and want isolated projects.
[07:23] Maya Chen: Redwood supports orgs/projects separation — you can have separate role sets per project and map SCIM groups to project-scoped roles. For stronger separation consider Dedicated pools or Private.
[07:34] Priya Kumar: on cert rotation again — what about automated notification of expiring certs?
[07:38] Jordan Patel: we emit warnings via the console and via email to configured admins starting 30 days before expiry. For Private installs we can integrate with your monitoring system.
[07:48] Lina Gomez: audit log schema — can you show an example event?
[07:51] Jordan Patel: sure i'll paste in chat after the call; example: { timestamp, actor_email, actor_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, ip, request_id, details } — we can redact request body if necessary.
[08:06] Ethan Ross: sounds good. for the SCIM POC we'll need a dev account, what's the provisioning window?
[08:11] Maya Chen: we can stand up a dev account within 48 hours and provide temporary keys for the POC. Jordan will prepare the SCIM sandbox.
[08:19] Priya Kumar: one more compliance question — do you support SAML attribute encryption?
[08:23] Jordan Patel: SAML attribute encryption is supported if your IdP and SP both support it; it's less common but doable. we'll test in the dev tenancy.
[08:33] Maya Chen: ok recap — we'll share SAML metadata and role mapping template, Jordan sends SCIM POC plan and rate limit doc, and we'll provide SOC2/ISO artifacts. Aurora will share test tenant info and group list. Any final?
[08:46] Lina Gomez: no, thanks all — this was helpful.
[08:48] Ethan Ross: thanks.
[08:50] Maya Chen: great — i'll follow up in email with attachments and a calendar invite for the SCIM POC. bye.
